references.text: Jesus went up on the mountain to pray by himself, a parallel to Luke 6:12 where he also goes up on the mountain to pray.
Luke also tells us here that Jesus withdrew to pray, showing his habit of seeking prayer in solitude.
Once again Jesus is alone in prayer, this time just before he asks the disciples who people say he is.
Jesus went up on the mountain to pray, and during the prayer he was transfigured – again showing the connection between mountains, prayer, and important events.
In Gethsemane Jesus prayed intensely through the night before his suffering, a parallel to the nighttime prayer in Luke 6:12 before an important decision.
Jesus rose early in the morning and went to a deserted place to pray, showing his regular practice of prayer.
Mark's parallel account of the selection of the twelve apostles, which took place after Jesus' prayer on the mountain.
The immediate continuation where Jesus chooses the twelve apostles after praying through the night, showing that prayer was preparation for this decisive choice.
Christ offered up prayers and pleas with loud cries and tears, reflecting the deep prayer life of Jesus as we see in Luke 6:12.
The psalmist prays evening, morning, and at noon – a parallel to Jesus' perseverance in prayer throughout the night.
Jacob wrestled with God through the night, an Old Testament parallel to spending the night in prayer and seeking God's will before a decisive event.
Matthew's account of the selection of the twelve, which complements Luke's description of the preparation through prayer.
